body: You bang a spoon on a bowl. It makes a brilliant noise. You would like to check that result another twenty times.
result: You keep banging until you drop the spoon. You look very pleased with yourself.

body: You pull off one sock. There was a foot in there the whole time. The other sock now looks suspicious.
result: The sock catches on your heel. You keep trying for a while.

body: Ruby points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.
choice: Turn around at the crucial moment
result: Ruby gets a photograph of your hair. You have already found something else to do.

body: You draw a letter and slide it into a cardboard box. It comes straight out of the missing bottom. The postal service is extremely fast.
choice: Fold a bottom for the box
result: The letter stays inside this time. You open the box to make sure it arrived.

body: You can pull a jacket’s zip down perfectly. Getting it started in the other direction appears to require a different kind of engineering.
choice: Look closely at the little teeth
result: Two rows of teeth join as the slider moves. You inspect them from both sides.

body: Jack slips in front of you in the queue for the slide. Apparently knowing you is a transport policy.
result: The argument holds up the whole queue. Neither of you gets the next turn.

body: You start a practice race before Ruby blows the whistle. You are winning by an enormous amount.
result: You run again with everyone else. It is harder when they are moving too.

body: Jack starts a petition to make a damp sock the class mascot. Ruby asks what values the sock represents.
result: You help sketch a mascot everyone can sit near.

body: Jack offers to swap a plain cracker for your favourite snack. They describe it as “an incredible deal”.
result: You both get a taste. The cracker remains unpopular.

body: A familiar top now stops well above your wrists. Either you have grown or somebody has moved the ends.
choice: Compare it with an older photograph
result: The top looks the same. Your arms have been busy.

body: Jack keeps stopping during a music rehearsal whenever someone walks past. They ask whether you can stay for one more run-through.
result: They talk about feeling watched. You listen before offering advice.

body: Your list for the evening contains more tasks than the evening appears to contain hours. Writing smaller has not helped.
choice: Try to do everything at once
result: You move between tasks without finishing much. The list looks much the same when you stop.

body: Isla assigns debate sides by drawing names. You must argue against an idea you support. Jack looks delighted with the arrangement.
result: You find a better objection than you expected. Your speech becomes more careful about its claims.

body: Isla has put you and Jack down to tidy the classroom after an activity. You both thought the other person had volunteered.
choice: Ask Isla how the roster works
result: Isla explains the rotation. You help this time and know when your next turn is.

body: Isla sets a family-history interview. You call Ruby with one question about school. Twenty minutes later, they are still describing the journey there.
choice: Keep interrupting to speed things up
result: Ruby stops telling the long stories. Your notes are shorter than you hoped.

body: You stack three blocks. For a moment, the tower stands. Then you discover what your elbow has been planning.
choice: Build it again with a wider bottom
result: The new tower survives your elbow. Your hand brings it down a little later.

body: Helena points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.
choice: Wave at the small person on screen
result: The small person waves back. Helena joins in from behind the phone.

body: You put on what you think is your jacket. Your hands vanish into the sleeves. Gabriel is looking for theirs.
choice: Insist you have suddenly grown smaller
result: Gabriel points to the name inside. It is a fairly strong argument.

body: Your classroom display has Gabriel’s label under your drawing and yours under a picture of a potato. Arthur is about to show the class.
result: Arthur swaps the labels before the display. The potato keeps its anonymity.

body: Gabriel offers to swap a plain cracker for your favourite snack. They describe it as “an incredible deal”.
result: Gabriel eats the cracker. You enjoy your snack.

body: Gabriel asks you to share a class project. Arthur has given you two months. That sounds like a problem for Future You.
result: Gabriel appreciates knowing before the deadline. You do not make a promise you cannot keep.

body: You are asked to introduce yourself to a room full of people your age. Your mind supplies every fact except your name.
choice: Take a breath and keep it simple
result: You say your name, add one true thing, and sit down. Adequate is underrated.

body: You borrow Helena’s charger and find it in your room several days later. Your room appears to have extended the loan.
choice: Agree on a place to return borrowed things
result: You return the charger and choose a visible spot for future returns. Remembering remains your part of the arrangement.

body: Arthur has put you and Gabriel down to tidy the classroom after an activity. You both thought the other person had volunteered.
result: Gabriel finishes alone. They and Arthur both notice your early departure.

body: There is a baby in the mirror. They copy every move you make. You have concerns about their manners.
result: They pull it right back. You laugh and try another one.

body: Your voice echoes in a stairwell. Whoever lives in the walls knows the same words as you, but always says them late.
choice: Wait for the walls to start
result: Nothing happens. Whoever is in there appears to be waiting for you too.

body: You turn a cardboard box into a rocket. Camille says dinner is ready. Mission Control has terrible timing.
result: Camille puts one foot in the box. The rocket is now full.

body: Your pocket contains three stones, a leaf and something that used to be a leaf. You are considering opening a museum.
result: The stones return to the path. You can still visit them.

body: Sophie invites you to a birthday party at an arcade. The invitation has more glitter than useful information.
result: You thank Sophie. You can still spend time together at school.

body: At assembly rehearsal, Jamie asks you to test the microphone. You say “Is this thing on?” The empty hall asks it back.
result: You slow down and read it through. Jamie asks you to keep that pace.

body: It is your turn at show-and-tell. The thing you meant to show is at home. Sophie has noticed your empty hands.
result: You nearly knock over a chair. The class remembers the demonstration.

body: You and Sophie invent a secret language. By lunchtime, neither of you remembers the word for lunch.
result: The conversation becomes much easier. You keep one secret word for emergencies.

body: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

body: Someone keeps making a joke out of Sophie’s name. Sophie has stopped correcting them.
result: Sophie tells you it has been bothering them.

body: Camille plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.
result: Camille turns it up. This may have strengthened the opposition.

body: After a class announcement, Sophie whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.

result: Most people heard the first comment. You prevent a second one.

body: You can pull a jacket’s zip down perfectly. Getting it started in the other direction appears to require a different kind of engineering.
choice: Put it down and take a break
result: The jacket lies beside you. You give your fingers a rest before another attempt.

body: You tell Hannah there is a dragon under your blanket. Hannah asks whether it would like a bedtime story.

result: The dragon listens very quietly. Hannah does all the voices.

body: At the library, you find a book so big you need both arms to carry it. The return desk suddenly looks very far away.
choice: Find a smaller story you love
result: You read it twice. The ending works both times.

body: Emil opens a lunchbox with nothing in it. They look embarrassed. Hannah is nearby.
result: Hannah sorts out lunch. Emil asks why you had to tell everyone.

body: Your pocket contains three stones, a leaf and something that used to be a leaf. You are considering opening a museum.
result: The smallest stone gets its own section. The crumbled leaf needs a larger display area.

body: Hannah steps around a shelf in a shop. You turn the other way and suddenly cannot see them.
choice: Ask a member of staff for help
result: A member of staff helps you find Hannah. You are both relieved.

body: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.
result: For once, being indoors feels like the plan.

body: After a class announcement, Emil whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.
result: Finn turns it off for you. Neither of you is asked to make the next announcement.

result: You agree who will do each part. Complaining takes longer than the last few chairs.

result: You practise responding without interrupting. Emil finds the weak parts of your opening.

body: Mateo points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

result: Mateo keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

body: In a quiet shop, you loudly announce that Mateo has a bottom. Several shoppers appear to know already.
result: Mateo hugs you back and changes the subject.

body: You ask Mateo whether you can camp in the living room. Your packing list contains six cushions and no clothes.
choice: Help make a proper sleeping spot
result: Mateo helps you set up, then checks on you before bed.

body: You are losing a board game with Mateo. You have just remembered a rule under which you would be winning.
choice: Insist it has always been the rule
result: Mateo opens the instructions. Your amendment is difficult to locate.

body: Your classroom display has Hugo’s label under your drawing and yours under a picture of a potato. Valeria is about to show the class.
result: Hugo laughs and helps switch the labels. Your drawing gets its own name back.

result: It is impressive. Valeria moves the microphone out of reach for the moment.

body: Hugo practises a recorder beside you. The tune sounds like a kettle being threatened.
result: You slow the tune down. It improves after several attempts.

body: Lucía finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

result: Lucía agrees not to show it to visitors. You keep the option of laughing at it yourself.

body: You tell Lucía you will stop playing after this round. The game helpfully begins another round before you have finished the sentence.
result: Lucía points out how many times you have said it. The argument lasts longer than the final round.

body: Lucía plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.
choice: Ask what it reminds them of
result: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Lucía.

body: Lucía sends a voice message. The wind gets most of the speaking time. You can make out your name and something about later.
choice: Arrange a time to talk properly
result: You speak when you can both hear each other. The original message was mostly a question about your day.

body: You turn a cardboard box into a rocket. Chloé says dinner is ready. Mission Control has terrible timing.
result: You reach zero, make a loud noise and land beside the table.

body: You knock Chloé’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.
result: Chloé handles the sharp pieces. You help find a safe new use for what remains.

body: Gabriel asks a question. You know the answer. Waiting for your hand to be noticed feels like a serious design flaw.
result: They explain a step you had done in your head. It turns out to be useful.

body: A familiar top now stops well above your wrists. Either you have grown or somebody has moved the ends.

body: Chloé finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

result: You agree on a section to write. The deadline is saved; agreeing has not completed any work.

body: Chloé sends “Where are you?” You are somewhere perfectly ordinary, but the fourth message arrives before you finish typing.

body: You draw a huge purple person on the wall. Amelia walks in while you are adding the teeth.
result: You clean the part you can reach. The teeth are higher up.

body: A caterpillar is crossing a path. It has a lot of feet and very little urgency.
result: You reach the end of the path first. Your opponent appears unaware of the result.

body: One of your old teddy’s button eyes comes off. You ask Amelia whether teddy needs an ambulance.
result: Amelia handles the needle. You choose where the eye belongs.

body: A loud fart interrupts the lesson. Grace looks straight at you. Their face suggests a serious conflict of interest.

result: Amelia asks you to stop. Grace denies everything with remarkable confidence.

body: Amelia asks for volunteers to play a tree in the class show. The tree has one line: “I am a tree.”

result: Amelia notices the identical wrong date and asks you to redo the assignment.

result: You agree to save the playlist for a break. The work finally starts moving.

body: Rohan sends you a photo of tomorrow’s homework answers. Their message says “delete after reading”, which sounds very normal.

body: Aarav is halfway through a story when you notice their phone in their hand. You may have found a witness for your next argument about phones.

result: Its name takes three attempts to pronounce. Its tax arrangements remain unclear.

result: Lorenzo stays beside you until the haircut is done.

body: Rain keeps your class inside at break. Leonardo proposes a board game, then explains a rule you are fairly sure they just invented.
result: The rules are ridiculous in both directions. You finish the game laughing.

result: The leaf receives a title too, despite its condition.
